Makes my skin smoth. Good.

it dries me out. My skin since having my daughter has changed from oily to combination/dry. column11: Never though I would use oil as a cleanser

column10: For context, I am a huge skincare junkie. I used to have severe acne, mostly under control after much education and research into my skincare routine. I was enticed by DE?ôs lovely packaging and messaging, but so far 3/4 products I have tried (C-Firma, B-Hydra, Lala Retro) have been overpriced and underwhelming. This particular cream I was hoping would bolster my skin barrier with its ceramides - I was a bit skeptical of its oil contents as they lack clinical evidence, but thought I would give it a chance given the raving reviews. I used for just over two weeks daily before returning. First it burned a little when I put it on, likely minor irritation from one of its ingredients - NOW I know that this is a personal reaction, so let us skip over this one. Second, over the two weeks I noticed no change in my skin barrier (measured by how oily I get, how dry my skin feels mid-day how sensitive my skin is to its usual products, how much I flake, etc). I know a lot of my issues may be personal, and it is a fine moisturizer. But at 100$ I expect it to do more than my 20-30$ moisturizers, and it really did not. I returned to my evidence-based La Roche Posay Cicaplast Baume B5 for my barrier needs - by the same standards above, my skin improved in less than a week. Yes, it may be less cosmetically elegant than DE, but it did its job at a much lower pricepoint. I cannot justify ever recommending this product, unless you literally have money to spare. After a couple years of giving DE a chance, I am disappointed in them as a brand for setting this kind of price point without much clinical evidence to back it up. Surveys and paid/product provided reviews are not evidence. I have learned my lesson. I would recommend Paula?ôs Choice as a brand to explore if you have not yet. A pleasant surprise from Glow Recipe for me, most notably in the fragrance (or lack thereof), and the beautiful way in which this serum goes on. This serum did sit wonderfully under makeup, but my honest favorite usage was for a bare face. The ingredients list is solid, but the 5 weights of HA seems a bit gimmicky to me. I did not see or feel a difference in hydration performance compared to other HA serums I have used. The antioxidants are a nice bonus, as is the collagen, but their effects are primarily seen long term. Having used the heavily fragranced watermelon and pineapple glow products in the past I was VERY surprised by the barely detectable hint of plum scent in this. If you are like me, and sensitive to fragrances skincare, this serum is absolutely worth a shot. Ultimately, if you are looking for a simple HA serum, there are plenty of other plainer, cheaper multi-molecular weight formulas to try. What sets this product apart is the addition of the antioxidants and the fabulous application that leaves you with the dewy, but not greasy look that is so desirable and well nourished skin.
